existing.description: The Leiden University Excellence Scholarship is a study scholarship for excellent students joining a full-time Leiden University master's programme starting in September, with the exception of the non-advanced LLM and MSc programmes of Leiden Law School. Applicants must normally hold a non-EEA/non-EFTA passport and not be eligible for Dutch student finance. The scholarship is awarded for the duration of the programme at one of five tuition-fee levels between EUR 10,000 and EUR 19,000, and Leiden states it is not a full scholarship, so a significant personal contribution is still required and non-EEA recipients must prove sufficient funds for their residence permit. The application is made inside the master's admission application with a motivation letter of maximum 500 words, and the deadline is 1 December 2026.
eligibility: Apply to a full-time Leiden University master's programme starting in September

Hold a non-EEA/non-EFTA passport and not be eligible for Dutch student finance (Studiefinanciering); exceptions for all LLM Advanced Studies programmes and the MSc in International Relations and Diplomacy, which have no nationality restriction
Excellent academic results in the previous study programme, indicated as being amongst the top 10% of graduates
Not already hold a Leiden University master's degree, except where a specific previous master's programme or work experience is mandatory
UK nationals are eligible because the UK is a non-EEA country, with an exception for applicants registered in the Dutch BRP before 1 January 2021
existing.eligibility_summary: Students with a non-EEA/non-EFTA passport, not eligible for Dutch student finance, who apply to a full-time Leiden University master's programme starting in September and have excellent academic results (top 10% indication).
benefits: Tuition-fee contribution for the full duration of the master's programme
coverage: One of five tuition-fee award levels: EUR 10,000, 15,000, 17,500, 18,500 or 19,000
Awarded for the duration of the study programme
No living-cost, travel or insurance coverage
requirements: Submit an admission application to the master's programme first
In the scholarship section of the application, indicate the intention to apply for the LExS
Upload the LExS motivation letter of maximum 500 words
Submit the scholarship application before the LExS deadline; no changes or emailed additions are possible afterwards
documents: LExS motivation letter as a PDF of maximum 500 words
Complete master's admission application and application fee payment where applicable
Written confirmation of agreement with the LExS terms and conditions before the award
existing.english_requirement: Not set by the scholarship; the chosen master's programme sets its own English language requirements.
application_method: Apply online for admission to the Leiden University master's programme and pay the application fee where applicable
Return to the Apply screen and open the Scholarships section
Select the LExS and upload the motivation letter
Submit the scholarship application before the deadline
existing.selection_notes: Faculty selection committees nominate LExS recipients within 10 weeks of the deadline and all applicants are notified before the end of March. Leiden has around 25 LExS scholarships a year against more than a thousand applicants, so the award is highly competitive.
existing.best_fit: Academically outstanding non-EEA/non-EFTA applicants to an eligible September-start Leiden master's programme who can still cover the remainder of tuition, living costs and their visa financial requirements.
existing.notes: Applying to more than one study programme or specialisation requires a separate LExS application and motivation letter inside each admission application. The award level is final and non-negotiable once granted.
existing.application_period: Annual round tied to the September intake; the scholarship application is made inside the master's admission application, with faculty selection committees nominating recipients within 10 weeks of the deadline and results notified before the end of March.
existing.deadline_display: "Deadline 1 December 2026" for master's programmes starting in September. "Late scholarship applications will not be considered."
existing.program_type: University excellence scholarship for incoming non-EEA/non-EFTA master's students

existing.description: The University of Groningen's NL Scholarship is a one-time grant for international students from outside the EEA who wish to pursue a master's degree in the Netherlands, co-funded by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science and the university. It amounts to EUR 5,000, is awarded for one academic year only and can be received only once in a lifetime, and it is intended to help cover living expenses during the first year of study rather than to cover the full cost of studying. Applicants need an admission offer for one of the listed master's programmes, a bachelor's degree obtained outside the Netherlands and excellent undergraduate performance, and they must submit a motivation letter, a transcript of records and the admission letter before the deadline. The published deadline for the 2026-2027 academic year was 1 February 2026, with results notified by 15 March.
eligibility: Do not hold the nationality of an EEA country and not be eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for any other reason
Enrolled at the University of Groningen as a full-time student for the academic year and master's programme for which the scholarship is awarded
Bachelor's degree obtained or to be obtained outside the Netherlands, with no diplomas from the Netherlands and no previous education in the Netherlands (exchange programmes are excluded)
Demonstrated excellent academic performance during the bachelor's studies
Hold an admission offer letter from the University of Groningen for one of the programmes on the published applicable-programmes list
Be eligible to meet the requirements for obtaining a Dutch student visa
Not have obtained the NL Scholarship before
existing.eligibility_summary: Non-EEA students admitted to a full-time master's programme on the University of Groningen's list, with a bachelor's degree obtained outside the Netherlands, excellent undergraduate performance and eligibility for a Dutch student visa.
benefits: EUR 5,000 granted once, in the first year of study
coverage: One-off grant of EUR 5,000 to contribute to living costs in the Netherlands
Awarded for the first academic year only
No tuition, travel or insurance coverage
requirements: Receive an admission offer from the University of Groningen for a listed programme first
Complete the scholarship application form on the official page
Upload the motivation letter, transcript of records and admission letter
Submit before the published deadline; incomplete applications are not considered
documents: Motivation letter outlining academic goals and how studying in the Netherlands fits future plans
Transcript of records of all undergraduate courses so far
(Conditional) admission letter from one of the listed University of Groningen master's programmes
existing.english_requirement: Not set by the scholarship; the chosen master's programme sets its own English language requirements.
application_method: Apply for and receive an admission offer for an eligible master's programme
Complete the NL Scholarship application form on the University of Groningen site
Upload the motivation letter, transcript of records and admission letter
Submit the application before the deadline
existing.selection_notes: Recipients are selected on academic excellence, ambition and relevant experience, assessed by the faculty selection committee of the programme applied for; the University aims to notify all applicants by 15 March.
existing.best_fit: Non-EEA students with an admission offer from an eligible University of Groningen master's programme and a strong, well-documented undergraduate record.
existing.notes: The stored title also mentioned a Talent Grant; no Talent Grant appears on the University of Groningen's official NL Scholarship page, so that part of the title could not be verified. Students already enrolled at the University of Groningen who want to study or do research abroad are directed to a separate outbound NL Scholarship page in the staff portal.
existing.application_period: Annual cycle tied to the master's admission round; applications open after the applicant receives an admission offer, with a 1 February deadline for the 2026-2027 academic year and results notified by 15 March.
existing.deadline_display: "The deadline for the 2026-2027 academic year is 1 February 2026 (23:59 CET)." The page had not been updated with a 2027-2028 deadline when checked on 2026-10-04.
existing.program_type: Government and university co-funded one-time grant for incoming non-EEA master's students
